newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks start weak, seen consolidating.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks start weak, seen consolidating.

text.p: Greek shares were soft in early trading, shedding 0.17 percent, and brokers said they expected stocks to consolidate today and stage a recovery next week.

"I think we will some consolidation today and a recovery next week when the market will have absorbed the shock of higher interbank rates and the poor performance of OTE OTEr.AT which has adversely affected sentiment," said Nick Kapatos, broker at Nexus Securities.
Depos and forex forwards firmed in early dealings on a liquidity squeeze linked to forex outflows on Tuesday and Wednesday but the drachma was stronger against the ecu and bonds were little changed.
Sales of blue chips by foreign funds accounted for a large part of the bourse's retreat in the last few days, said Kapatos.
"I am sure we will see tham back when the money market situation clears and companies start announcing good interim results," he added.
The Athens general index was down 0.31 percent or 4.89 points to 1,551.57 from Thursday's 1,556.46 close after 35 minutes of trading, recovering from a 1,553.93 intra-day low.
Turnover amounted to 1.4 billion drachmas on volume of 0.34 million shares.
Advances lagged declines 45 to 53 with 18 shares unchanged on 116 traded.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas, capped at 5,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,112-1,142 drachmas.

The recently launched second Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 6,800 drachmas, capped at 10,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,038-1,098 drachmas. The warrants expire December 16, 1998. Shares of the underlying stock were down 5.0 drachmas at 6,190.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted at 602.39-640.84 drachmas. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $70.65-$73.41. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted at 3,314-3,532 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $11.66-N/O. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted at 222-253 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998.
